label: prf:variational-equations
title: Proof of Variational equations of the categorical action
html:
Proof. Proof of Variational equations of the categorical action

Each equation is obtained by computing \delta\mathfrak{S}_q = 0 with respect to the indicated variable, using the non-degeneracy of \int_A.

Item (1): Vary \int_A. The gravity term \mathrm{tr}(q \cdot R_{\int}) depends on \int_A through the Frobenius--Ricci endomorphism R_{\int}. Varying \int_A \mapsto \int_A + \delta\!\int_A and requiring \delta\mathfrak{S}_q = 0 for all \delta\!\int_A gives, by non-degeneracy of the categorical trace, R_{\int} - \tfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{tr}(R_{\int})\mathrm{id}_A = T_q[\nabla, \psi], where the stress-energy T_q collects the \int_A-dependence of the gauge and matter terms. The trace subtraction ensures \mathrm{tr}(T_q) = \tfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{tr}(R_{\int}) (the contracted Bianchi identity).

Item (2): Vary \nabla. The gauge term \int_A \circ \mathrm{tr}_A(F_\nabla \wedge_q \star_q F_\nabla) depends on \nabla through F_\nabla = \nabla^2. A standard computation using \delta F_\nabla = \nabla(\delta\nabla) and integration by parts (via non-degeneracy of \int_A) yields \nabla \star_q F_\nabla + q \cdot [F_\nabla, \star_q F_\nabla] = J_\psi. The commutator term q \cdot [F_\nabla, \star_q F_\nabla] arises from the non-commutativity of the q-deformed wedge product; it vanishes when q = 1 (the abelian/classical limit).

Item (3): Vary \psi. The matter term \int_A(\psi^* \cdot D_\nabla\psi) is linear in \psi. Varying \psi \mapsto \psi + \delta\psi and using (\delta\psi)^* \cdot D_\nabla\psi = 0 for all \delta\psi gives D_\nabla\psi = 0 by non-degeneracy of \int_A and the dagger structure (positive definite dagger).
